rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 6 lowered kp from 2.0 to 1.6 and scored 51.18, a large fall from the iteration 5 best of 75.78. Progress dropped on every track (oval 0.29 to 0.115, s-bend 0.153 to 0.150, slalom 0.108 to 0.108), and the oval fell hardest. The kp trend therefore turned over: kp 2.0 is the best raced gain, and the monotonic-trend assumption from the iteration 6 rationale is rejected. Every run still ends off track with one line-loss event and max_error about 0.062 to 0.067 m, above the 0.06 m limit. Oscillation stays low (0.08 to 0.16), so the robot drifts to an edge rather than weaving. Gain changes have now been tried at 1.6, 2.0, 2.5, and sensor span and speed have been varied, with no change to the one-loss-per-run failure.

Change. I revert kp to 2.0 (the iteration 5 design, 75.78) and keep everything else identical: base_speed 1.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, search_right, sensor weights, and sensor x positions at -0.04, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.04. The only change is sensor_size from 0.012 to 0.016. This follows the fallback branch the Evaluator and iteration 6 both named. With a 16 mm footprint, edge sensors should keep seeing tape to a larger lateral offset, and the readings should be less blind near the edge before the 0.06 m limit. The sensor layout is otherwise unchanged, so the effect can be attributed to footprint size.

Expected result. Progress should match or exceed iteration 5 (oval about 0.29, s-bend about 0.15, slalom about 0.11). line_loss_events may fall, and max_error may drop below 0.06 m if the edge is reached because the outer sensors lose the tape too early. If progress falls or the signal becomes noisy, revert to sensor_size 0.012.

Hypotheses. H9: the 12 mm footprint leaves the outer sensors blind before the off-track limit, and the 16 mm footprint extends detection range. H10: the kp optimum sits near 2.0 at this speed and sensor geometry. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, plus whether the loss point moves along the course.
